Hi Elena —

Thanks again for taking the call yesterday. Attached is our redline of the Order Form and the publicity/press language we typically propose. High-level items we want to surface so legal can review in parallel: 

- Confidentiality carveout for mutually agreed press announcements and customer list inclusion (we propose prior written approval for any quote or case study).
- Logo use: marketing must approve final assets; logo usage window is limited to the active term + 6 months unless otherwise agreed.
- Jurisdiction: our standard is California law; your redline asked for the customer to pick — please confirm whether BlueArc can accept CA or require contract-level opt-in.
- Evidence: external customers often request SOC2 / audit evidence before public mention; we've included a simple checklist in the redline.

Can you loop in your procurement/GC and let us know any hard no's? If anything is time-sensitive for your launch window, flag the dates and we'll prioritize.

Attachments: BlueArc_OrderForm_Redline_v1.pdf (pdf)

Next steps: if your counsel provides markup, Laura (cc'd) will consolidate and propose final language for the MSA+Order Form.

Best,

Hannah —

Thanks for the redline and for the clear summary. Quick notes from our side before I send this to procurement/GC: 

1) Jurisdiction: our legal team prefers to keep governing law as the customer location (i.e., our contracts are typically governed by UK law for EMEA customers). Is Redwood open to an exception per customer location?

2) Publicity: we can accept customer lists and logo use for the standard marketing channels, but we need a 30-day embargo from any PR announcement to allow internal comms review.

3) Logo approvals: BlueArc requires final logos to be delivered as SVG/PNG and reviewed by our brand team. Can you add that to the Order Form as a required step?

4) Evidence: Tom (cc) will circulate a SOC2 evidence checklist — we typically require it for press permission on product-specific case studies.

I'll wait for Tom's note and then get procurement to return a markup.

Best,

Elena —

Thanks — that all sounds reasonable. A couple of quick proposed compromises to keep things moving: 

- Jurisdiction: we can accept a customer-choice governing law where required by local procurement (i.e., BlueArc can have UK law apply), but we will request venue neutrality for injunctive relief and will keep our main dispute contact in Santa Clara — Laura, happy to work on one-line language here.
- Embargo: 30 days is fine for public PR. For referenceable customer lists (e.g., product and platform partners), we ask for written opt-in that can be automated via email confirmation from the customer's comms lead.
- Logo assets: we'll add a required deliverable in the Order Form: final logo files (SVG/PNG) and a single approval window (5 business days). Marketing will provide the final assets back to BlueArc for confirmation.

We'll incorporate the SOC2 checklist once Tom sends it. If BlueArc needs DocuSign executed before Nov 20 to meet a marketing milestone, let me know and I'll prioritize routing.

Cheers,
Hannah

Elena / Tom / Hannah —

Thanks for the quick back-and-forth. I've drafted clause text that reflects the compromises below — attaching as a short plain-text snippet for easy copy/paste: MSA_publicity_clause_suggested.txt (attached). Key points summarized: 

- Publicity & Reference Rights: Customer grants Redwood the non-exclusive right to include Customer name and logo in Redwood marketing materials, customer lists, and case studies solely with Customer's prior written approval (which will not be unreasonably withheld). Any product-specific quotes or case studies will require explicit written approval.
- Embargo: No public press or PR announcement by either party referencing the other's participation shall occur until 30 calendar days after the other party has delivered written approval of the content.
- Logo Use: Customer must deliver final logo files in SVG/PNG format; Redwood's Marketing will provide a single 5-business-day approval window. Redwood will not modify the logo beyond sizing and placement without prior consent.
- Governing Law & Venue: Unless Customer specifies otherwise at execution, this Agreement will be governed by the laws of the State of California. Notwithstanding the foregoing, where Customer is located in a jurisdiction that requires local governing law (e.g., UK/EU entities), the parties may elect that jurisdiction for that Customer's Agreement, with the exception that requests for injunctive relief shall be handled in a mutually agreed neutral forum or the Redwood principal place of business.

Please review and let me know any redline language from BlueArc's counsel we should incorporate. If Tom can share the SOC2 evidence checklist (or confirm it's in progress), I'll add the reference to the Order Form as an evidence item for publicity approval.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
